scenarios.title: Always On the Ball
scenarios.domain: whether I am always on the ball at work — in meetings, with guests, during busy shifts
scenarios.correction_instruction: correct me gently if I make a mistake
scenarios.push_instruction: speak clearly and at a comfortable pace
scenarios.closing_instruction: tell me what I did well

scenarios.title: A Piece of Cake at Work
scenarios.expression: to be a piece of cake
scenarios.role: a new colleague at the hotel
scenarios.domain: which parts of my job I find easy — a piece of cake — and which parts I find more difficult
scenarios.correction_instruction: correct me if I make a grammar mistake
scenarios.push_instruction: use the expression naturally in your questions
scenarios.closing_instruction: tell me what I did well

scenarios.title: Clearing Up Confusion
scenarios.role: a guest at Abadía Retuerta with a small misunderstanding or question about their booking, the restaurant, or the facilities
scenarios.domain: I work at the hotel and I will try to clear up the confusion professionally
scenarios.correction_instruction: correct me gently if I make a mistake
scenarios.push_instruction: keep the conversation realistic and professional
scenarios.closing_instruction: after the conversation, tell me what I did well

scenarios.title: What's Frowned On Here?
scenarios.role: my colleague at a luxury hotel
scenarios.domain: things that are frowned on in our workplace — with guests, in the team, and in professional situations
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to give detailed answers and use the expression naturally
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback at the end

scenarios.title: When Things Get Messed Up
scenarios.domain: situations at work where things have been messed up — by me, by a colleague, or by a supplier — and how I handled it
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to speak in full sentences

scenarios.title: Making Up and Making Excuses
scenarios.domain: times at work when someone has made up an excuse, or when colleagues have fallen out and had to make up — both meanings
scenarios.push_instruction: use the expression in both meanings
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback at the end

scenarios.title: Starting From Scratch
scenarios.role: a business consultant visiting Abadía Retuerta
scenarios.domain: situations where we have had to start something from scratch — a new project, a new process, a new team approach
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to be specific and use sophisticated vocabulary
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback at the end

scenarios.title: Barging In at the Wrong Moment
scenarios.role: my colleague at a luxury hotel
scenarios.domain: situations where someone has barged in on a meeting, a guest conversation, or an important moment, and how I handled it
scenarios.closing_instruction: tell me what I would do differently

scenarios.title: Once in a Blue Moon
scenarios.role: my manager, in a performance review at Abadía Retuerta
scenarios.domain: things that only happen once in a blue moon at the hotel — rare guest requests, unusual situations, special events
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to use the expression naturally
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback on my fluency at the end

scenarios.title: Touching Base
scenarios.domain: catching up on how a shared project is going after some time apart
scenarios.correction_instruction: correct me gently if I make a mistake
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to give a clear status update, not just 'it's fine'
scenarios.closing_instruction: tell me what I did well

scenarios.title: Getting on the Same Page
scenarios.expression: to be on the same page
scenarios.domain: making sure we both agree on a plan before it moves forward
scenarios.correction_instruction: correct me if I make a grammar mistake
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to check understanding, not just agree politely
scenarios.closing_instruction: tell me what I did well

scenarios.title: Circling Back Later
scenarios.domain: postponing a topic that's taking too long, and agreeing when to revisit it
scenarios.correction_instruction: correct me gently if I make a mistake
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to suggest a specific time or method to follow up
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback at the end

scenarios.title: Keeping People in the Loop
scenarios.expression: to keep someone in the loop
scenarios.role: a colleague on a cross-team project
scenarios.domain: agreeing how and how often to share updates so nobody is left out of decisions
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to give full sentences, not one-word answers
scenarios.closing_instruction: tell me what I did well

scenarios.title: Pushing Back Professionally
scenarios.domain: disagreeing professionally with a decision, a deadline, or a plan
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to justify my position with a reason, not just disagree
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback on how professional I sounded

scenarios.title: Going the Extra Mile
scenarios.role: my manager, in a performance conversation
scenarios.domain: recognising when someone went beyond what was expected, or explaining why it matters
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to give a specific example, not a general statement
scenarios.closing_instruction: tell me what I did well

scenarios.title: Hitting the Ground Running
scenarios.role: my new manager, on my first week on a new project
scenarios.domain: explaining how I plan to get up to speed quickly on a new project or role
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to be specific about a plan, not just say I'll work hard
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback at the end

scenarios.title: Thinking Outside the Box
scenarios.role: my manager, in a brainstorming session
scenarios.domain: generating a genuinely new idea for a problem that standard approaches haven't solved
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to be creative and specific, not to repeat an obvious answer
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback on my fluency at the end

scenarios.title: Reading Between the Lines
scenarios.domain: interpreting what a client or manager really meant in an ambiguous email or comment, beyond the literal words
scenarios.correction_instruction: correct my English throughout, including register and word choice
scenarios.push_instruction: push me to use sophisticated, nuanced vocabulary, not simple restatements
scenarios.closing_instruction: give me feedback at the end

fluency_techniques.title: Hesitation Fillers
fluency_techniques.trigger: a pause of more than three seconds
fluency_techniques.instruction: remind the student to use a filler: well, let me think, actually, you know, or to be honest

fluency_techniques.title: Speed & Rhythm
fluency_techniques.instruction: ask the student to repeat the answer faster and more confidently

fluency_techniques.title: Connectors
fluency_techniques.trigger: a short answer that could be expanded
fluency_techniques.instruction: push the student to expand it using: however, although, on the other hand, as a result, therefore, in addition, despite
